observation.what: On the source kernel, long back-pressure service is 8088 slots for both ordinary and lifting students. FIFO-full wait is 1159 vs 1903. Always-ready can differ (6914→6170 or 6938→5354 depending on construction). Tables are not additive.
observation.not: closed same-port net service of the full r1 chain

research_question: Which wait class accounts for the 8088 long-BP slots, and does that class live in the source-only kernel or only in a dual-consumer kernel?

candidates.statement: The 8088 is the contracted output FIFO / blocked-receiver waveform of the source kernel (896/1024 unready). PED last-use is not in this kernel.
candidates.prediction: Infinite sink drops both students below 8088; lifting may keep an always-ready advantage; dual-consumer kernel may show a different stall mix.
candidates.incompatible_if: Infinite sink still yields 8088 on the source kernel.

candidates.statement: Producer cannot retire until continuous PED/I24 last-use completes (H1/G1).
candidates.prediction: On a dual-consumer kernel, wait tags are dominated by PED_BP and s_done vs r_done lag is nonzero.
candidates.incompatible_if: Source-only 8088 is unchanged with infinite sink, or dual-consumer lag histogram is ~0.

candidates.statement: Live full-domain proj BN is the stall.
candidates.prediction: BN wait appears only after projection; source-kernel 8088 has zero BN tag.
candidates.incompatible_if: Source-kernel tags show BN_barrier as the mass (would indicate a mis-instrumented kernel boundary).

candidates.statement: Instruction/RF/ROM structure, not last-use of either tensor.
candidates.prediction: Tags land in other; changing last-use policy does not move 8088.
candidates.incompatible_if: Typed last-use policy moves same-port service ≥15% at matched AEE.
